meeting_header:
Date: 2025-02-14
Time: 16:00 - 16:52 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood CSM); Jared Kim, Anita Rao, Marcus Chen, Leah Rivera (OpalFlare)
summary: Kickoff for OpalFlare's implementation of Redwood Inference. Goals: confirm deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security requirements (SSO, SOC2, KMS/HSM), pilot scope (throughput, latency SLOs), and next steps for sample data and benchmark runs. Decided: start with a hosted pilot with VPC peering option; security deep dive scheduled. Pricing and onboarding materials to be shared.
topics: Current infra & network (VPC, egress, private endpoints)
Pilot scope: perf targets, dataset, prompt set
Deployment options (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, we'll run through what success looks like for OpalFlare and then hand over to Liam for technical intake.
[00:12] Jared Kim: Hi all, Jared here, VP Eng at OpalFlare. We're kicking off inference integration for our support summarization and routing flows.
[00:20] Anita Rao: Anita, head of ML. We'll own the prompt sets and eval.
[00:24] Marcus Chen: Marcus, security. I'll cover compliance needs.
[00:28] Leah Rivera: Leah, DevOps, I'll handle network stuff.
[00:32] Maya Chen: Awesome. Goal for today: align on pilot scope, deployment constraints, security asks, and owners. Liam?
[00:36] Liam O'Connor: Yeah thanks. Quick overview: Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC / on-prem). For pilots we usually recommend hosted to move fast then iterate to Dedicated or Private if you need isolation.
[00:50] Leah Rivera: Just to flag — we are constrained by corporate egress policy. Anything that needs internet egress has to be via our proxy. We also prefer private endpoints if possible.
[00:58] Priya Patel: Noted — we can capture that in the network checklist. Maya will share.
[01:03] Jared Kim: Our SLOs: 95th perc latency for generation should be under 300ms for short replies, and we expect ~300 reqs/sec during peak. Cost is important but latency is the main gating factor.
[01:18] Liam O'Connor: Okay, good to know. For 300 qps and low latency, we usually tune batching and KV-cache settings. Quick note: our KV cache — sometimes the transcript has it as K-V cash — it's the same thing.
[01:30] Anita Rao: Can you explain how Redwood handles model fallbacks? If a specific model is down or overloaded, what happens?
[01:36] Liam O'Connor: Sure. Smart routing will route by policy — latency or cost. We'll set a fallback chain: primary model -> quantized variant -> smaller/cheaper model. That keeps the app up. We can also set automatic degrade thresholds.
[01:50] Marcus Chen: Security questions: do you support SSO/SAML, RBAC, tenant-level audit logs, and BYOK with KMS or HSM?
[01:58] Maya Chen: Yes to SSO/SAML, RBAC in the Console, and audit logs. For KMS — we support customer-managed keys for Private deployments and in Dedicated through a KMS integration; hosted can integrate with customer KMS if required, we'll get you the details.
[02:12] Marcus Chen: We'll need to see SOC2 and pen test reports. Also how long logs are retained and whether we can configure retention.
[02:20] Priya Patel: We'll attach the security pack and SOC2 report in the follow-up.
[02:24] Leah Rivera: On networking, is there a VPC peering option for hosted or is that only Private?
[02:29] Liam O'Connor: Hosted supports private endpoints and VPC peering in certain regions — we'll include the network diagram. If you need full on-prem, the Private package is the option.
[02:38] Jared Kim: For the pilot, we want to validate end-to-end — real prompts, measure latency, and sanity-check hallucination rates. We want to run a 2-week pilot. Is that standard?
[02:48] Maya Chen: Totally reasonable. Two-week pilot with 1-2 model variants. We'll instrument prompts and evals. The Optimize toolkit can give quantization recommendations if you want to trade cost/latency.
[02:59] Anita Rao: Do you support streaming responses for our chat UI?
[03:03] Liam O'Connor: Yes, streaming and function calling. For low latency UI we recommend streaming + prefix caching.
[03:10] Jared Kim: About data retention — we don't want any customer PII stored in any logs.
[03:14] Marcus Chen: Right, must be able to opt-out of retention or have strict redaction.
[03:18] Maya Chen: We have configurable retention and can do zero-retention on request for certain routes. We'll include configuration notes.
[03:25] Leah Rivera: On the infra side, what are the egress IPs we need to allow?
[03:28] Liam O'Connor: We'll send a list; for hosted there are ranges per region, also private endpoints reduce egress.
[03:34] Anita Rao: For the pilot perf runs, what telemetry do you recommend we capture?
[03:38] Liam O'Connor: Token-level latency, request/response traces, and per-route cost breakdown. We'll give you an instrumentation snippet — SDK or REST. Also sample load runner configs.
[03:50] Jared Kim: Any blockers migrating from our current model infra? We're using an internal inference service on Kubernetes with custom serving.
[03:57] Liam O'Connor: No blockers — we can integrate with your pipeline. Many customers start with hosted API to compare perf/cost then move to Dedicated when they commit. If you want to stay on-prem, we can package Private.
[04:09] Marcus Chen: About encryption in transit — TLS is a given, but do you support mTLS for private endpoints?
[04:14] Liam O'Connor: Yes, mutual TLS is supported on Private and Dedicated. Hosted supports TLS; we can evaluate mutual TLS for specific enterprise setups.
[04:24] Maya Chen: Quick commercial note — we can provide pilot credits for the POC; I'll include pricing ranges in the follow-up.
[04:31] Jared Kim: Great. Who will be the day-to-day contact from Redwood during pilot?
[04:34] Priya Patel: That will be me for CS coordination, Liam for technical, and Maya for account.
[04:40] Leah Rivera: Can you walk through a sample onboarding checklist?
[04:43] Maya Chen: Sure — Step 1: access & SSO; Step 2: network (VPC, ip allowlists); Step 3: sample payloads and test harness; Step 4: perf runs and debugging; Step 5: roll to prod. We'll send the checklist.
[04:58] Anita Rao: For evaluation, we want unit-level QA: precision/recall of reranking and hallucination metrics. Does Redwood have eval tooling or do we bring our own?
[05:06] Liam O'Connor: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. You can bring your own eval harness too. We'll share the eval templates.
[05:16] Jared Kim: Any known limitations with long sequences? Our docs summarization can hit 4k token windows.
[05:21] Liam O'Connor: Runtime supports modern attention optimizations and can select kernels based on sequence length. For 4k windows we'll recommend certain model variants and quantization profiles. We'll include recommendations.
[05:33] Marcus Chen: Are there SOC2 covered requirements for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[05:38] Maya Chen: Both have compliance controls; Dedicated adds reserved capacity and stricter isolation; Private is the most compliant for regulated workloads. We'll outline specifics in the security pack.
[05:49] Leah Rivera: On deployment cadence, we want a canary rollout plan and automatic fallback to a lighter model if latency spikes. Is that supported?
[05:57] Liam O'Connor: Yes, rollout policies include canary percentages, A/B, and automatic fallback to compatible model variants when capacity is constrained.
[06:07] Anita Rao: For the pilot data, do you need de-identified examples or raw logs?
[06:11] Maya Chen: De-identified preferred, but if you need to send raw we can accept under NDA — we'll coordinate with legal.
[06:18] Jared Kim: Timeline: ideally run pilot next week for 2 weeks and have a decision meeting after. Is that feasible?
[06:23] Maya Chen: Yes, we can. Action items and deck in 3 business days.
[06:27] Marcus Chen: Also request a short questionnaire on key controls so we can pre-check with our compliance team.
[06:32] Priya Patel: We'll include a 1-page security questionnaire.
[06:35] Leah Rivera: One more — what's the process for secrets management? We use HashiCorp Vault.
[06:40] Liam O'Connor: We integrate with common secret managers; Vault is supported for retrieving API keys in Private and Dedicated. Hosted can also be configured with vault via connectors.
[06:49] Anita Rao: Quick question — do you have examples of customers who began on hosted then moved to Dedicated?
[06:54] Maya Chen: Yes, several. We'll include anonymized case studies in the follow-up.
[06:59] Jared Kim: Okay let's recap next steps.
[07:02] Maya Chen: Recap: Maya will send onboarding deck, network + SSO checklist, security pack (SOC2, pen tests) by Feb 18. Liam will request sample payloads and design pilot perf tests by Feb 21. Anita will provide prompt set and expected SLOs by Feb 20. Marcus will deliver SOC2 and KMS notes by Feb 20. We'll schedule a security deep dive in the week of Feb 24.
[07:25] Leah Rivera: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[07:28] Maya Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up in email with links: Onboarding deck (link), Security pack (link), Pilot runbook spreadsheet (link).
[07:36] Jared Kim: Thanks. End.
